#6046. Progressive advocates call on House Democrats to force Cuba vote

Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, D-N.Y., is the sponsor of a Cuba war powers resolution filed in May. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

Progressive advocates are urging House Democrats to force a vote during the lame-duck session on a resolution aimed at preventing war against Cuba, arguing the issue is too urgent to wait until Democrats control the chamber next year.

“The Cuban people are suffering and dying, and cannot afford further months of inaction,” 50 progressive groups wrote to Democratic House leaders in a letter dated Wednesday. “In the midterm elections, U.S. voters resoundingly rejected a foreign policy of war and domination, and made clear their desire for Congress to act forcefully to rein in the Trump administration.

Holding a vote would demonstrate that Democrats recognize the urgency facing the Cuban people, and would help set the tone for an assertive agenda of peace, diplomacy and respect for international law in the 120th Congress, the letter added.

At issue is a war powers resolution introduced in May by Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, D-N.Y., and House Foreign Affairs Committee ranking member Rep. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., that would call on the president “to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Cuba, unless explicitly authorized by a declaration of war or a specific authorization for use of military force.”

The letter was sent to House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, Meeks and House Rules Committee ranking member Jim McGovern, D-Mass. It was signed by prominent anti-war groups such as Win Without War, Just Foreign Policy, the Friends Committee on National Legislation, Indivisible and Code Pink.

Advocates are frustrated that House Democrats have not forced a vote on a Cuba war powers resolution even as they have forced multiple war powers votes on Iran and see it as an example of leadership that is at odds with the progressive wing of the party. One advocate who requested anonymity to speak candidly said it’s their understanding Democratic leaders are hesitant to make potentially vulnerable Florida members of the caucus vote on the issue.

Spokespeople for Jeffries and Meeks did not respond to requests for comment Wednesday on whether Democrats will force a vote before the end of the year, what their reasoning is if they don’t and whether they plan to bring up a vote next year.

Senate Democrats sought to force a vote on a similar resolution earlier this year, but Republicans in that chamber successfully derailed the effort. Senate Republicans raised a point of order that the resolution was not entitled to privileged status under the War Powers Resolution since U.S. troops aren't actively engaged in combat against Cuba. The point of order was sustained in a mostly party-line vote of 51-47.

Senate Democrats later introduced another Cuba war powers resolution, which they have not tried to force a vote on and have not signaled they will do so before the end of the year.

The resolutions have come amid several veiled threats from President Donald Trump suggesting eventual military action against Cuba.

“I want to get Cuba done before I leave,” Trump told conservative radio host Hugh Hewitt last week when asked if he would order the use of military force against Cuba.

“Frankly, I’d love to be able to do it for the people, for the Cubans that came and were treated really badly, and they came to America,” Trump said, adding he would “certainly consider” taking military action.

Trump’s comments are on top of a pressure campaign his administration has been waging against Cuba. Since January, the United States has imposed a blockade of oil shipments to the island, causing fuel shortages that have led to lengthy blackouts and aggravated an economic crisis.

While the Senate vote in April did not go Democrats’ way, advocates still saw it as sending a strong message.

“Despite falling short of the majority, this was among the strongest votes in congressional history against the use of blockades, and one of the most important stands Congress has taken against U.S. economic sanctions toward Cuba in over six decades,” the letter from progressive organizations said. “The House should take a similarly forceful action at this crucial moment.”

The House vote, even if successful, would be largely symbolic since the measure Democrats can force a vote on is a concurrent resolution. Concurrent resolutions are widely considered to be nonbinding even if cleared by both chambers of Congress since they do not get a presidential signature, though anti-war advocates dispute that applies to war powers.

The progressive groups in their letter called for “decisive leadership” in forcing a vote on the issue.

“Across the political spectrum,” the letter said, “Americans do not want another regime change war, nor an open-ended, nation-building project abroad based on false pretenses — especially not when escalation risks exposing the United States to new national security risks, placing US servicemembers in harm’s way, stoking regional instability, and becoming the latest chapter in a long history of harmful U.S. regional policies that have fueled mass migration to U.S. shores.”

Delta Air Lines and American Express offer seven cobranded cards for everyone from occasional Delta flyers to frequent travelers.

Here’s how the current offers compare and what to consider before applying.

Apply for the : Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 125,000 bonus miles after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.

The following is a comparison of the various welcome offers currently available. Note that TPG values Delta SkyMiles at 1.2 cents per mile as of November 2026. This valuation assumes you're using your miles to book flights with Delta or one of its partners.

American Express has a few eligibility rules to keep in mind before applying for one of these cards. For starters, Amex typically only allows a person to earn one welcome bonus per card in their lifetime. That means you'll want to prioritize applying when a card offers an elevated, limited-time offer, such as the ones all but one of these cards have right now.

You also may not be eligible for a welcome bonus on a personal Delta Amex card if you have or previously had a higher-tier Delta Amex card. For example, if you have or previously had the Delta Reserve Amex, you may not be eligible for the welcome offers on the Delta Blue, the Delta Gold and the Delta Platinum.

Delta's business Amex cards are not subject to this same "family rule."

Amex may consider other factors, including your income, your credit score and your history with the issuer, when determining your eligibility. Fortunately, you'll generally find out whether you're eligible for a welcome offer before accepting the card.

Related: A complete guide to Amex's 1-bonus-per-lifetime restrictions

Delta offers four personal cards. The card that is right for you depends on how frequently you fly with Delta and how much you’re willing to pay for an annual fee.

Let’s take a look at what differentiates each of the Delta SkyMiles personal cards.

Best for: Delta loyalists or those who want Sky Club access (subject to limitations).

The is ideal for hardcore Delta fans and frequent flyers.

Current welcome offer: Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 125,000 bonus miles after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.

This bonus is worth up to $1,500, per our valuations.

If you qualify for the full 125,000 miles, this is an excellent time to apply. It matches the highest mileage bonus we’ve seen on the card and requires $1,000 less in spending than the previous 125,000-mile offer with the lowest spending requirement.

Key benefits: Delta’s premium consumer credit card offers a range of valuable perks. For loyal Delta flyers who enjoy visiting the Sky Club, this card can pay for itself through lounge access, spending boosts and other benefits. If you're chasing status with Delta, the Delta Reserve's Medallion Qualification Dollar head start and earning boost make it a very compelling option.

With this card, you’ll earn 3 miles per dollar spent on Delta purchases made directly with the airline. Plus, you'll enjoy a slew of Delta-related perks, including:

To learn more, read our full review of the Delta SkyMiles Reserve.

If you fly frequently with Delta but can’t justify the pricier Delta SkyMiles Reserve, the is worth considering.

Current welcome offer: Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 90,000 bonus miles after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.

Per TPG's valuations, this bonus is worth up to $1,080.

If you qualify for the full 90,000 miles, this is a strong offer for $3,000 in spending. We’ve seen offers with more miles or a statement credit, though they required more spending.

Key benefits: This card is a good option if you fly Delta regularly and want to earn miles on purchases and reach elite status. The Delta Platinum is a good choice for status chasers who want an extra boost but don't want to pay the Delta Reserve's steep price tag.

However, even if you aren’t pursuing status, the companion certificate alone can make the annual fee for this card worth it.

With this card, you’ll earn 3 miles per dollar spent on Delta purchases made directly with the airline.

To learn more, read our full review of the Delta SkyMiles Platinum.

Best for: Occasional Delta flyers or those test-driving a Delta card.

If you want to take advantage of a welcome bonus but don’t fly Delta frequently, the is a strong option.

Current welcome offer: Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 80,000 bonus miles after spending $2,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.

TPG's valuations place this bonus at up to $960.

If you qualify for the full 80,000 miles, now is a good time to apply. However, we have seen up to 90,000 miles — as well as up to 80,000 miles plus a statement credit — offered before.

Annual fee: $0 introductory annual fee for the first year, then $150.

Key benefits: This card is ideal for occasional Delta flyers seeking a few extra perks when flying with the airline.

With this card, you’ll earn 2 miles per dollar spent on Delta purchases made directly with the airline.

To learn more, read our full review of the Delta SkyMiles Gold.

If you want an entry-level card to start earning SkyMiles and fly less frequently with Delta, then the is the card for you.

Current welcome offer: Earn 10,000 bonus miles after spending $1,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership.

According to TPG’s valuations, these miles are worth $120. The SkyMiles Blue typically doesn't receive an elevated offer, so we recommend applying whenever you're ready.

Key benefits: As a no-annual-fee card, it offers fewer benefits than the others. Still, there are some simple perks for cardmembers.

With this card, you’ll earn 2 miles per dollar spent on Delta purchases made directly with the airline.

To learn more, read our full review of the Delta SkyMiles Blue.

If you own a small business or have a side hustle through which you pay business expenses, one of these offers may be a great addition to your work wallet.

#6043. Tempers flare as future of Social Security debated

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday showed how poisonous the politics could become.

Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day. Democrats erupted, accusing Johnson of scaring seniors and being unwilling to fix a financial lifeline for more than 72 million retirees.

“I think it’s outrageous,” said Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., one of several Democrats on the panel who slammed Johnson for his comments. “Don’t go out there scaring Americans to make political points on Fox News. This is too fricking important.”

Johnson acknowledged making an “imprecise comment” on prospects for a fix during the Fox interview. But he also told Democrats that if they had read his “chairman’s memo” he sent them Tuesday they would know he wants to preserve the system and pass a law to prevent any cuts to benefits if the Social Security Trust Fund is depleted.

"This is a scam, it’s grotesque, and at this point there’s really no way to fix Social Security," he said on Fox Business. "It’s a Ponzi scheme. You can’t fix it. You just shut it down and hope you can recover some of your money.”

But Johnson appeared to contradict himself later in the same interview, saying there is a difference with a “government-sanctioned Ponzi scheme” in that “you can force investors to keep putting money into it and that’s what we’ll probably have to do … You can fix Social Security and make it solvent.”

In his opening statement at the hearing, Johnson said Congress should pass a law to prevent benefit cuts and then “roll up our sleeves and begin seriously addressing the main problem, our massive debt and deficits.” He said that is the only way to “ensure we have the financial wherewithal to honor promises made to seniors.”

Johnson also told the panel he used the term “Ponzi scheme” in part to draw attention to the importance of addressing the problem. “If I gotta pay a political price for that, I really don’t care,” he said.

There is no doubt that a fix is needed. Without any change, Social Security recipients face a 22 percent cut in benefits by the end of 2032, according to projections from the Social Security Board of Trustees. Johnson said Congress and the president won’t cut benefits even if the trust fund is exhausted.

And there has been no shortage of Social Security bills introduced to provide a fix, but none of them has gained momentum.

Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, drew flak from fellow Republicans after he and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., proposed lifting the cap on income subject to the Social Security payroll tax so that the tax would apply to all earned income.

A bipartisan proposal, from Sens. Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., Bill Cassidy, R-La., Tim Kaine, D-Va., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, would have put a plan in motion by requiring the Social Security Advisory Board to recommend a bill that would ensure Social Security is funded for at least the next 50 years.

Senators on both sides of the aisle said they were committed to fixing Social Security. Republicans stressed the importance of economic growth to bring in more revenue to the system and cautioned that tax increases would slow growth.

Democrats pitched shifting more revenue into the system, for example by raising the cap on the payroll tax or taxing other income.

“I do believe if we can be focused on fixing the Social Security stability issue, that could be a stepping stone to fixing broader problems,” said Kaine, who is anticipated to chair the Budget Committee when Democrats take over Congress next year.

#6042. Hakeem Jeffries’s Reckless Medicare Expansion

House Minority Leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D., N.Y.), flanked by Minority Whip Rep. Katherine Clark (D., Mass.) and Rep. Pete Aguilar (D., Calif.), leads a press conference after an incoming wave of House Democrats voted to nominate him as their leader in the next Congress, on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., November 18, 2026.

We have long warned that if Republicans did not get serious about advancing their own vision for health care, Democrats would use their next opportunity to further expand the role of government. And here we are.

Fresh off a sweeping victory in the midterm elections, incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries made a radical proposal. He endorsed lowering the retirement age of Medicare and adding vision, hearing, and dental coverage to the program. Additionally, he said that the government should provide coverage for all children.

No doubt, with a stampede of new socialists joining his caucus, Jeffries is trying to get ahead of the left-wing push for a fully government-run system branded as “Medicare for All.” When last nationally debated in 2019, it was estimated to add $34 trillion to existing federal spending with no plausible financing mechanism.

At this point, Jeffries’s proposal is theoretical. There’s a big budgetary difference between lowering the Medicare eligibility age from its current 65 to 60, and lowering it to 50 — as Senator Kirsten Gillibrand and other senators are proposing. There are also questions about what sort of premiums, if any, would be required for near-retirees to “buy in” to the program or how generous the theoretical vision, hearing, and dental benefits would be. Filling in those blanks is the difference between a proposal that costs a few hundred billion dollars and one that costs trillions of dollars.

But it’s preposterous at this stage to start any discussion of Medicare with a suggestion that spending on the program needs to be increased rather than reined in — especially to cover a population without a high uninsured rate. Over the next decade, the federal government is projected to spend $18.5 trillion on Medicare, making it the largest expenditure apart from that other federal entitlement, Social Security. Medicare no longer collects enough money in payroll taxes to cover current benefits, let alone added benefits that cover more people. Even a more modest lowering of the retirement age to 60 would add over 7 million beneficiaries. On its current trajectory, Medicare’s trust fund (the money it is “owed” by the rest of the government from the days when it was running surpluses) would be exhausted by 2033.

Medicare is a major driver of the nation’s broader fiscal problem. Already, debt held by the public has eclipsed 100 percent of gross domestic product. By the end of the decade, it is projected to reach 120 percent. By comparison, debt peaked at 106 percent during World War II. Now we are on track to exceed that number, not during a global crisis, but during an ordinary period of relative peace and prosperity. And that’s before Jeffries grabs the gavel with a massive majority behind him.

Perhaps more concerning, President Trump indicated last week that he may be game for some compromise proposal. “There is a real possibility that we get a lot of great things done, especially on health care,” he said.

If Trump is serious and actually considers cutting a deal with Democrats to expand Medicare, congressional Republicans should fight it at all costs.

The Editors comprise the senior editorial staff of National Review magazine and nationalreview.com.

#6041. Woman Faced A Felony Charge For Stealing A Rental Car—Then Won A Seat In Congress And Prosecutors Dropped The Case

This year was such a wave election that in some cases candidate quality didn’t matter at all. It was enough to win just not to be a Republican. Shortly before the election, Democratic congressional candidate LaKesha Womack pulled into a high school parking lot in North Carolina for a Sunday rally. A sheriff’s deputy pulled up behind her. He handed her a felony summons for stealing a Toyota Corolla she’d rented from Budget nearly seven years earlier. The incumbent congressman she was running against turned the rental into a television ad. She won anyway. And on Tuesday, after Budget got paid for the six weeks its car was overdue, the district attorney dropped the charge for good. It’s good to get elected to Congress. Budget Car Rental Got The Corolla Back In 2019 Womack picked up the car in Charlotte on August 27, 2019, and renewed the rental twice. Her last extension began October 7, 2019. According to the police report the vehicle was due back at noon on October 23. On November 26 an officer reported that police couldn’t find her and put out an all points bulletin. Police recovered the Corolla and returned it to Budget on December 4, 42 days late. Budget sold the vehicle the following year. Womack has a number of excuses for never returning the car. She says a diabetic seizure and long hospitalization had wiped her out financially. (It’s not clear why that kept her from returning it.) Her son went into foster care while she was in the hospital (again, unclear why that kept her from returning it) and the two of them wound up living in a hotel (hotels have parking, but the hotel didn’t force her to keep the car). She’d expected the company to come get the car. She says she had nowhere reliable to receive mail (when you rent a car you know you’re supposed to give it back, even without a mailed notice) and she thought the matter was settled (exactly how it would have been is unclear). On January 14, 2020, a court issued a summons for felony failure to return the car. Under North Carolina law, willfully keeping a rental vehicle past its deadline is a felony if the vehicle is worth more than $4,000. The car was valued at $20,000. Womack says she first heard about the case on Friday, October 9, 2026. A local reporter posted the records. She responded, “I do owe them people some money, obviously.” BREAKING: Documents pulled from the NC Courts government website show District 14 congressional candidate Lakesha Womack has a “pending” felony warrant for failure to return a rental car in 2019. Police records say Budget Car Rental rented a car to Womack on Oct. 7, 2019 and it was supposed be returned on Oct 23, 2019. Pics and links attached. https://t.co/4WZRvweFxM — Brett Jensen WBT News (@Brett_Jensen) October 9, 2026 Two days later, on October 11, the summons was reissued. A Polk County deputy’s body camera caught the handoff outside the county Democratic rally. Republican Congressman Tim Moore ran an ad on this. Watch Tim Moore’s campaign ad, “Keep Your Money.” He Helped Draw The District. She Didn’t Even Live In It. Moore spent ten years as speaker of the North Carolina House, helped gerrymander the district to favor Republicans and won it in 2024 by nearly 65,000 votes. Womack, an ordained minister making her first run for public office, lived in a neighboring district and said she had no plans to move. A House member only has to live in the state. Through October 14, Moore had spent $1,921,880 to Womack’s $55,626. He spent nearly $1 million on ads. She had no paid full-time staff and didn’t buy a TV spot. Three days after the deputy served her she was handing out T-shirts to striking workers at Charlotte Douglas airport. Moore won five of the six counties. He even won the Election Day vote by 21,246. But early in-person voting, which started four days after the deputy showed up, gave Womack a 24,700 vote lead. With the felony case still pending, she posted, “#HatersGonnaHate I’m still Congresswoman-Elect.” On November 16 prosecutors learned she’d reached a deal with Budget. She paid the assessed rental cost for the overdue period. Budget told prosecutors it was satisfied. Campaign donations may not have mattered in the race, but that’s an unusually inexpensive way to buy goodwill with a member of the U.S. House of Representatives. On November 24 the state dismissed the charge with prejudice. This Wasn’t Hertz When I first wrote about Womack on October 11, my entire comment was “Ruh roh – it wasn’t Hertz.” A reader guessed Budget had lost track of a car it already had back. A father and his 13-year-old daughter were held at gunpoint outside Savannah in a car they’d just rented from Hertz’s Thrifty brand. When police let the father show them his rental agreement, it was 36 minutes old. The car had been reported stolen before Thrifty handed him the keys. A Hertz President’s Circle member wound up in jail over a Salt Lake City rental he’d extended, returned and paid $3,900 for. Those arrest stories seemed to dry up after Hertz brought in Palantir to help track its fleet in 2022 and agreed to pay $168 million to settle 364 claims. At Least Womack Was Still Campaigning North Carolina Republicans drew a map they expected would give them 11 of the state’s 14 U.S. House seats. Democrats won 11. Elsewhere the wave carried a couple of candidates who’d actually stopped campaigning. In Iowa, Eric Armstrong suspended his state House campaign on September 7 for health reasons. He beat a county supervisor and retired police lieutenant by about ten points. In Texas, Ericka Lomick suspended her campaign when a federal mortgage fraud conviction raised questions about whether she could serve. Her name stayed on the ballot for both the rest of the outgoing state representative’s term and the next one. She beat the same Republican in both elections. He’s asked the Texas Supreme Court to block certification of the special election. In California, Womack’s $55,626 would’ve looked like a fortune to Hipolito Cerros. The 28-year-old former mayor raised no campaign money, hired no staff and bought no ads. He unseated the Republican leader of the state Assembly. Tennessee tech support worker Victoria Broderick lost to Congressman Scott DesJarlais in 2024. He took 70% of the vote. After Republicans redrew the district, she ran again. She was still working full time and had to message her boss the morning after the election. The race was called for her the same day Womack’s charge was dropped. My personal favorite this cycle is Maricopa County, Arizona’s Sebastian Matta – a 19-year-old Arizona State philosophy sophomore – who beat a former state senator to become clerk of the Superior Court. He’d filed his campaign finance paperwork late and blamed his accountant for going quiet on him. He’ll run an office that processes 15,000 documents a day. To rent a Corolla from Budget at the Phoenix airport, he’s still two years short of the usual minimum age. In 2012, the anti-gay Democrat running as the incumbent for state representative in Hutchinson, Kanasa defeated her primary challenger – an openly gay son of a former member of the Ku Klux Klan – and then went on to best her Republican opponent who was a pro-gay rights, pro-choice train conductor named Dakota Bass. That race was featured in season two, episode eight of The Newsroom. (HT: Paul H.) My personal favorite this cycle is Maricopa County, Arizona’s Sebastian Matta – a 19-year-old Arizona State philosophy sophomore – who beat a former state senator to become clerk of the Superior Court. He’d filed his campaign finance paperwork late and blamed his accountant for going quiet on him. He’ll run an office that processes 15,000 documents a day. To rent a Corolla from Budget at the Phoenix airport, he’s still two years short of the usual minimum age. In 2012, the anti-gay Democrat running as the incumbent for state representative in Hutchinson, Kanasa defeated her primary challenger – an openly gay son of a former member of the Ku Klux Klan – and then went on to best her Republican opponent who was a pro-gay rights, pro-choice train conductor named Dakota Bass. That race was featured in season two, episode eight of The Newsroom. (HT: Paul H.) Topics on this pageBudget Rent a CarLakesha WomackUnited States CongressUnited States House of RepresentativesArizonaCaliforniaCharlotteDemocratic PartyHertzIowaNorth CarolinaPhoenixRepublican PartySalt Lake CityTennesseeTexasThe NewsroomThrifty Car Rental+14 more More From View from the Wing

Womack picked up the car in Charlotte on August 27, 2019, and renewed the rental twice. Her last extension began October 7, 2019. According to the police report the vehicle was due back at noon on October 23.

On November 26 an officer reported that police couldn’t find her and put out an all points bulletin. Police recovered the Corolla and returned it to Budget on December 4, 42 days late. Budget sold the vehicle the following year.

Womack has a number of excuses for never returning the car. She says a diabetic seizure and long hospitalization had wiped her out financially. (It’s not clear why that kept her from returning it.) Her son went into foster care while she was in the hospital (again, unclear why that kept her from returning it) and the two of them wound up living in a hotel (hotels have parking, but the hotel didn’t force her to keep the car). She’d expected the company to come get the car.

She says she had nowhere reliable to receive mail (when you rent a car you know you’re supposed to give it back, even without a mailed notice) and she thought the matter was settled (exactly how it would have been is unclear).

On January 14, 2020, a court issued a summons for felony failure to return the car. Under North Carolina law, willfully keeping a rental vehicle past its deadline is a felony if the vehicle is worth more than $4,000. The car was valued at $20,000.

Womack says she first heard about the case on Friday, October 9, 2026. A local reporter posted the records. She responded, “I do owe them people some money, obviously.”

BREAKING: Documents pulled from the NC Courts government website show District 14 congressional candidate Lakesha Womack has a “pending” felony warrant for failure to return a rental car in 2019. Police records say Budget Car Rental rented a car to Womack on Oct. 7, 2019 and it was supposed be returned on Oct 23, 2019. Pics and links attached. https://t.co/4WZRvweFxM

— Brett Jensen WBT News (@Brett_Jensen) October 9, 2026

Two days later, on October 11, the summons was reissued. A Polk County deputy’s body camera caught the handoff outside the county Democratic rally. Republican Congressman Tim Moore ran an ad on this. Watch Tim Moore’s campaign ad, “Keep Your Money.” He Helped Draw The District. She Didn’t Even Live In It. Moore spent ten years as speaker of the North Carolina House, helped gerrymander the district to favor Republicans and won it in 2024 by nearly 65,000 votes. Womack, an ordained minister making her first run for public office, lived in a neighboring district and said she had no plans to move. A House member only has to live in the state. Through October 14, Moore had spent $1,921,880 to Womack’s $55,626. He spent nearly $1 million on ads. She had no paid full-time staff and didn’t buy a TV spot. Three days after the deputy served her she was handing out T-shirts to striking workers at Charlotte Douglas airport. Moore won five of the six counties. He even won the Election Day vote by 21,246. But early in-person voting, which started four days after the deputy showed up, gave Womack a 24,700 vote lead. With the felony case still pending, she posted, “#HatersGonnaHate I’m still Congresswoman-Elect.” On November 16 prosecutors learned she’d reached a deal with Budget. She paid the assessed rental cost for the overdue period. Budget told prosecutors it was satisfied. Campaign donations may not have mattered in the race, but that’s an unusually inexpensive way to buy goodwill with a member of the U.S. House of Representatives. On November 24 the state dismissed the charge with prejudice. This Wasn’t Hertz When I first wrote about Womack on October 11, my entire comment was “Ruh roh – it wasn’t Hertz.” A reader guessed Budget had lost track of a car it already had back. A father and his 13-year-old daughter were held at gunpoint outside Savannah in a car they’d just rented from Hertz’s Thrifty brand. When police let the father show them his rental agreement, it was 36 minutes old. The car had been reported stolen before Thrifty handed him the keys. A Hertz President’s Circle member wound up in jail over a Salt Lake City rental he’d extended, returned and paid $3,900 for. Those arrest stories seemed to dry up after Hertz brought in Palantir to help track its fleet in 2022 and agreed to pay $168 million to settle 364 claims. At Least Womack Was Still Campaigning North Carolina Republicans drew a map they expected would give them 11 of the state’s 14 U.S. House seats. Democrats won 11. Elsewhere the wave carried a couple of candidates who’d actually stopped campaigning. In Iowa, Eric Armstrong suspended his state House campaign on September 7 for health reasons. He beat a county supervisor and retired police lieutenant by about ten points. In Texas, Ericka Lomick suspended her campaign when a federal mortgage fraud conviction raised questions about whether she could serve. Her name stayed on the ballot for both the rest of the outgoing state representative’s term and the next one. She beat the same Republican in both elections. He’s asked the Texas Supreme Court to block certification of the special election. In California, Womack’s $55,626 would’ve looked like a fortune to Hipolito Cerros. The poor people of NC, having this criminal “representing” them.

Summarizing: – Woman didn’t return rental car as per her contract. (Theft? Conversion? Breach of contract? The first two are criminal.) – Prosecutor drops carges [coincidentally?] once she’s elected – Woman shows no remorse

I’m confident if I got the summary wrong someone will correct me.

#1: I’m going for Theft as a minimum, police report justified, and prosecutor charges as well. Later had her attitude been better than “well maybe I should have returned THEIR car” (paraphrased) maybe walk it down to breach of contract or misunderstanding.

#2: Her getting elected changes no facts on the ground. She rented a car. She signed a rental contract. She failed to abide by it, and “kept the car” beyond her right to keep that car. The prosecutor rightly carged her, but the story doesnt seem to indicate WHICH charges were filed? And yet once elected the prosecutor dropped the charges. Why? (that’s a whole lot of question involving a who, a why, and a why now and not before or after.)

Is this justice? I I rent a car and don’t return it and the cops stop me I should be overjoyed to stay alive. Apparently she’s in a “better class of people” who can jocularly opine that maybe she should have returned the car.

I don’t know whom she represents, but I didn’t vote for her, and wouldn’t.

WAIT! So she’s actually a case where the person DID steal the car, and THIS is the time the rental car company decides to drop it.

I’m here for the comments defending her keeping the car.

Hmmmm . . . sitting on this for 7 years AFTER they recovered the car. I’m sure this is entirely coincidental and had nothing to do with the election. This is one of the clearest cases of a simple civil matter at this point for monetary damages. No chance in hell there wasn’t some political instigation to any criminal charges suddenly becoming alive again nearly 7 years after they got the car back.

@David – the felony summons was issued six years ago. The felony wasn’t invented because she was running for Congress. She stole a car!

When she got caught she write the car rental company a check and claims she had diabetes so it’s ok for her to steal a car. Democrats are indeed above the law!

Keeping the car, or simply failing to return the car for a while?

This looks like the latter. A whole bunch of problems, returning the car wasn’t high on her priorities. It was returned, I do not see criminal **intent**, I see someone overwhelmed. I doubt I would vote guilty, but I doubt I would vote for her in the election. This was not exactly good judgment.

L3 The poor people of the United States having a criminal leading them.

Bold decision-makers that aren’t afraid of taking risks tend to make great leaders.

She is likely a one term event and will draw a primary opponent next cycle It was a yellow dog election — people voted for anything that was not an R.

Shit happens. When shit happens to poor people, it happens a lot worse.

Now, do I know that her excuses are legit or not? I do not. But in our country, if you are living paycheck to paycheck like most American workers, and you get sick, and you are hospitalized, you lose everything, and you have to prioritize, and maybe not returning a rental car is your least bad choice of all your bad choices – especially if you were hospitalized for something as simple as not being able to afford your insulin.

Is that what happened? No idea. Is that would could have happened? Is our healthcare “system” destroying the lives of hundreds of thousands of WORKING Americans each year a thing? Yes it is.

Run a company that steals millions from their customers with fake fees or signing you up for fake accounts and you get to force your customers into individual binding arbitration if they want it back. Keep a rental car too long and we jump to throwing that person in prison for years.

Also, is the North Carolina law REALLY that keeping a car past the return deadline is a felony? Surely there’s more to it than that? I did that last month when I postponed my flight a day. Hertz added a day to my bill.

Lastly, if this were a random white man, nobody would bat an eye if a rental car company accepted payment of the past-due balance over charging them with a felony. Most of you are only mad because of the picture.

Going from criminal to successful politician. Donald Trump has set the standard that others now follow.

Lock her up!!! Lock her up!!! Lock her up!!!

Borrowing with no intention of ever giving it back? She’s a perfect fit for any Congress!

Republicans have been ripping off the country for at least the last two years and think we’re too dumb to understand. Trump is the swamp personified.

Funny how you constantly criticize Hertz for them filing charges about rental car theft; claiming it’s all fake news. It can never be the dad, working mother, or professional’s fault. Yet when it involves a Democrat, a woman, or person of color then shame on them – they must have stole the car. Not defending the situation, but your reporting is off hard here.

@Realworld – No, the Congresswoman-elect *admits it*

Charlotte is on a political roll. Flying under the radar for now, despite what happened to Iryna Zarutska – victimized by a repeat violent criminal who had no business walking the streets and who has still not been charged for what we all saw. But they are valiantly fighting to not provide any compensation to Zarutska’s family. Thanks to leaders in Chiarlotte that value the lowlifes over the rest of us.

This woman is no exception; someone who actually DID steal a rental car. And yet they elected her to congress. Imagine how corrupt she’ll be given time in DC. Heck, the ones who don’t start out as car theives are corrupt – imagine what a career thief can do!

“Democratic congressional candidate LaKesha”

We have a government headed up by the world’s most successful graft specialist, constantly violating the Constitution and the laws. When there’s a tsunami, the wave brings in a few dubious characters. In this case the status quo was (and is until January) so abominable that a lopsided majority of Americans chose to stop overlooking the malfeasance and incompetence of the ones in charge; and voted for people – not all of them saints – who will replace some of the Members of Congress who have been slobbering all over themselves to be favored pet poodles for the rot at the top.

Just a few decades ago the question was “Is it right or wrong?” Then it became “Is it legal or illegal?”. Now it’s the following sequence: “Is it illegal?”, “Will I be identified?”, “Will I be arrested?”, “Will I be charged?”, “Will I be prosecuted?”, “Will I be convicted?”, “Will the penalty be meaningful?” and “Will the penalty be enforced?”. This doesn’t bode well if we want a functional society.

Mendocino, a small coastal town in northern California, has welcomed its first points property. The nearly 50-year-old Hill House hotel was renovated and reopened in June 2026 as Hill House at Trailborn Mendocino, Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy — making it the first and only member of a major hotel loyalty program in Mendocino proper. (The closest options are members of IHG One Rewards and Wyndham Rewards in neighboring Fort Bragg.)

The Mendocino Coast region is known for its charming small-town vibes, natural beauty and outdoor pursuits, so the Trailborn brand’s laidback nature lodge concept fits in here like a seal in nearby Mendocino Bay. I stayed three nights in late October to get a first look at the property (and the town, which is on TPG’s 2027 Where to Go list).

Nestled just a few minutes’ walk outside downtown Mendocino, Hill House at Trailborn Mendocino’s unassuming two-story buildings fit right in with the surrounding hotel scene. The design is inspired by nature — specifically, the redwood forests and tide pools of the surrounding Mendocino Coast — while still feeling modern and polished.

The grounds are bursting with native plants, many of them still in bloom when I visited in late October. Botanical art prints and zoological illustrations on the walls give a nod to the great outdoors, and curious guests can lose themselves in the lobby’s curiosity cabinet, a revamped relic of the original building. Visitors are encouraged to sign the guestbook with a stamp of a dried leaf or flower.

The hotel offers just 44 accommodations — relatively large for a Mendocino property — including 14 double queen rooms, 25 king rooms and 5 junior suites. Within each room type, travelers can choose to upgrade to features such as a balcony or deck, an ocean view or both.

My room, a spacious King Junior Suite Ocean View, felt like a relaxing retreat with its muted color palette of greens, browns and yellows and its cozy linen spa robes. After a day of exploring Mendocino, I enjoyed relaxing on the sofa, perusing the coffee table book Botanicum, and sampling locally made goodies from the snack basket and minibar (for a fee).

Trailborn Hill House has one on-site restaurant: Pizza Standard Time, a casual bar and diner offering mostly pizza, plus salads, charcuterie boards and small Italian bites like arancini. The fare was limited but tasty; my friend and I tried a pizza, salad, and local Husch chardonnay and were quite happy. It’s nice having a quick, casual meal available on-site in case you arrive late and tired from the drive, but it’s also just a few minutes’ walk to Mendocino if you want more options.

Like all Trailborn properties, this one offers a lobby convenience store called Hill House Wine & Grocer. Guests can purchase local drinks and snacks (mostly the kind you’d find on a charcuterie board), plus apparel, toys, candles with the property’s signature scent and other souvenirs.

The hotel also offered a small but delicious complimentary breakfast spread. As with everything else during my stay, the breakfast was high-quality yet unpretentious, with guests serving and bussing their own tables. Instead of having a designated breakfast area, guests can find a cozy spot to eat inside Pizza Standard Time or the attached Cabot Cove Detective Library, outside by one of the fire pits or back to their room.

However, this will change when Trailborn’s second Mendocino property, The Mendocino Hotel, opens in 2027. Instead of complimentary breakfast, Hill House plans to provide guests with a voucher to Moonwave, The Mendocino Hotel’s dining concept, which will serve “coastal comfort” food three meals a day plus drinks at the lobby bar.

If you didn’t realize you were in a small town, you will as soon as you interact with any of the hotel staff — everyone I spoke to, from front desk staff to custodians, was beyond friendly.

As for amenities, they align with the brand’s laid-back, outdoorsy style and with some of the things the Mendocino area is known for. You’ll find:

Located just a few minutes’ walk (or bike ride) from downtown Mendocino, Hill House at Trailborn puts guests in the heart of the town’s charming boutiques and varied dining and drinking scene. But you won’t get bored if you hang around the property, either.

Here are some of the on-site activities guests may want to try:

While Mendocino’s remoteness makes it a haven for crowd-weary travelers, it’s becoming easier than ever to reach thanks to recent roadwork funding and new direct flights to Charles M. Schulz–Sonoma County Airport (STS), including on Alaska Airlines, Delta and Southwest. That’s one reason Mendo made TPG’s 2027 Where to Go list.

But travelers can also fly into San Francisco International Airport (SFO), Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport (OAK) or Sacramento International Airport (SAC), which are a bit farther away but offer more flight options.

Depending on the airport you choose, you’ll need to rent a car and drive two to four hours to Mendocino.

Basic rooms start as low as $140 per night in the off-season, while my King Junior Suite Ocean View starts around $350 per night (though these prices can climb much higher on summer weekends). Award rates start at 48,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night, or you could redeem a 50,000-point free night certificate.

When booking, you’ll want to use one of the credit cards that earn the most points for Marriott stays, as well as one that possibly offers automatic Marriott Bonvoy elite status for value-added benefits. These include:

The information for the Marriott Bonvoy Bountiful card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

Hill House has three wheelchair-accessible rooms, including two double queens and one king; these feature accessible tubs and, in some cases, roll-in showers. The property and its parking lot are also wheelchair accessible. For hearing-impaired guests, a portable kit can be installed in any room.

As a points traveler who loves Mendocino, I’m thrilled to see the town’s first points property not only opening but thriving. As a traveler who appreciates unique stays and has experienced some of the town’s charming independent properties, I’m also glad that Hill House at Trailborn Mendocino has brought enough character to fit seamlessly into the local scene.

It seems the Trailborn brand — and Marriott Bonvoy — is betting big on Mendocino. Hill House is one of two Mendocino properties purchased by The Trailborn brand. The second, the 150-year-old Mendocino Hotel, is undergoing renovation and slated to open in 2027.

#6039. It Takes a Family

The answers aren’t political and institutional; they are deeply relational.

John Mulaney in Saturday Night Live’s “Sister” sketch

The recent Saturday Night Live “Sister” skit hit a nerve with its fake ad for a 24-hour elder-care service. The service is “completely free,” provided you’re the brother.

“My dad means the world to me,” it begins, with comedian John Mulaney narrating. “So, when I noticed him start to slow down, I knew I needed to get him the best care possible. I didn’t want to put him in a nursing home, but a private health aide could cost thousands a week. I didn’t know where to turn.”

#6037. Rove’s Black Friday Deals Offer Up To 55% Transfer Bonuses—Plus 10x On Hotels That Earn Points And Perks

Rove is offering up to 55% more miles when you transfer to five airline and hotel programs, along with 10 miles per dollar on hotel bookings that still earn hotel points, elite night credit and status benefits. For the hotel offer there’s no stay deadline, so you can book future travel on Black Friday and collect the higher earning rate. Rove is a standalone rewards program. You earn its miles through travel bookings, shopping, dining and gift cards, then redeem them for travel or transfer them to airline and hotel programs. There’s no particular credit card you need to carry. Most of these offers last just one day. Here’s the schedule Rove gave me: November 26–30: transfer bonuses and double referral bonuses, ending at 11:59 p.m. Eastern on Monday, November 30. Black Friday, November 27: the 10x Loyalty Eligible hotel offer, boosted shopping and gift card earnings, first hotel booking bonus and double qualifying miles. These end at 11:59 p.m. Eastern that night. 40%–55% Transfer Bonuses To Five Programs The same percentage bonus applies to Japan Airlines Mileage Bank, Air France KLM Flying Blue, Finnair Plus, Copa ConnectMiles and ALL Accor. Your Rove status determines the percentage. The four airlines normally transfer 1:1. Accor’s normal ratio is 1.5 Rove miles to 1 Accor point. Here’s what transferring 15,000 Rove miles gets you: Rove Status Bonus Airline Miles Or Avios Accor Points Member or Gold 40% 21,000 14,000 Platinum 50% 22,500 15,000 Diamond 55% 23,250 15,500 Those percentages already include the extra transfer bonus for Platinum and Diamond. Japan Airlines is worth looking at for its own flights and partner awards, including American Airlines and Alaska Airlines itineraries with three free stopovers. Rove offered everyone a 50% Japan Airlines transfer bonus in October, though. The 40% offer for most members is lower than that, while Diamond’s 55% is higher. Japan Airlines miles expire after 36 months, so a bonus doesn’t make them a good place to park miles indefinitely. Finnair is useful even if you don’t plan to fly Finnair. You can move Avios to British Airways at 1:1. Your Finnair account needs to be at least 30 days old before you can link it to another Avios program. Accor points are generally worth 2 euro cents each toward eligible hotel stays. The 15,000 Rove miles in the table therefore produce €280, €300 or €310 in hotel value, depending on status. Platinum effectively gets a 1:1 transfer to Accor during this promotion, and Diamond does slightly better. 10x Hotel Miles While Keeping Hotel Points And Benefits On November 27, new Loyalty Eligible hotel bookings earn 10 Rove miles per dollar. Rove says there are no property or rate exclusions within that category, and no promotional deadline to complete the stay. I’ve liked this feature since it launched. You can earn Rove miles while retaining hotel program points, qualifying nights and applicable elite benefits, along with the rewards from the card you use to pay. A $1,000 qualifying room subtotal earns 10,000 Rove miles. At 1.5 cents per mile, that’s $150 in additional travel value, before the hotel and credit card rewards. 5,000 Miles On A First Hotel Booking Has Different Rules Promo code BF500 adds 5,000 Rove miles to an eligible first Rove Rate hotel booking of $500 or more made on Black Friday. Join if you aren’t already a member and then take advantage of this. Rove clarified that you must never have booked a hotel through them before. Someone who’s already made a Loyalty Eligible reservation doesn’t qualify merely because this would be their first Rove Rate booking. An existing Rove account can qualify if it hasn’t booked a hotel. The code can combine with an eligible Rove elite hotel discount. However, Rove Rate bookings don’t earn hotel points or elite night credit, or guarantee hotel elite benefits. At exactly $500, the bonus adds 10 Rove miles per dollar to the booking’s standard earnings. I’ve covered a 5,000 mile first booking offer at the same spending threshold before. Double Qualifying Miles Includes Purchased Miles Boost Black Friday transactions that ordinarily earn qualifying miles will earn twice as many toward Rove status. Rove confirms that includes purchased Miles Boost and elevated earnings for elite members. For example, $1,000 in qualifying hotel spending at the promotional 10x rate generates 10,000 redeemable miles and 20,000 qualifying miles. The extra status credit doesn’t double the redeemable miles you can transfer or spend. Rove’s annual requirements remain: Gold: 50,000 qualifying miles and 5 qualifying transactions. Platinum: 125,000 qualifying miles and 10 qualifying transactions. Diamond: 250,000 qualifying miles and 20 qualifying transactions. Flat bonuses such as BF500’s 5,000 miles don’t ordinarily qualify, so they aren’t part of the doubling. Status earned for 2026 lasts through December 31, 2027. Travel counts toward the year it’s completed, while shopping and gift card purchases count by purchase date. A hotel stay ending in 2027 won’t be 2026 qualifying activity because it was booked in 2026. Higher Gift Card Earnings And The Full Shopping List Rove is offering up to 30% more miles on nearly all gift cards on Black Friday. A 30% increase would turn a 5x rate into 6.5x, for instance. (The actual rate depends on the gift card.) Rove sells gift cards marked for instant mileage earning which can help with this weekend’s transfer bonuses. You can join Rove and then you’re welcome to leave your referral link in the comments though note that this link is good for 1,500 points just for joining rather than the standard 500. Rove clarified that you must never have booked a hotel through them before. Someone who’s already made a Loyalty Eligible reservation doesn’t qualify merely because this would be their first Rove Rate booking. An existing Rove account can qualify if it hasn’t booked a hotel.

The code can combine with an eligible Rove elite hotel discount. However, Rove Rate bookings don’t earn hotel points or elite night credit, or guarantee hotel elite benefits.

At exactly $500, the bonus adds 10 Rove miles per dollar to the booking’s standard earnings. I’ve covered a 5,000 mile first booking offer at the same spending threshold before.

Black Friday transactions that ordinarily earn qualifying miles will earn twice as many toward Rove status. Rove confirms that includes purchased Miles Boost and elevated earnings for elite members. For example, $1,000 in qualifying hotel spending at the promotional 10x rate generates 10,000 redeemable miles and 20,000 qualifying miles. The extra status credit doesn’t double the redeemable miles you can transfer or spend. Rove’s annual requirements remain: Gold: 50,000 qualifying miles and 5 qualifying transactions. Platinum: 125,000 qualifying miles and 10 qualifying transactions. Diamond: 250,000 qualifying miles and 20 qualifying transactions. Flat bonuses such as BF500’s 5,000 miles don’t ordinarily qualify, so they aren’t part of the doubling. Status earned for 2026 lasts through December 31, 2027. Travel counts toward the year it’s completed, while shopping and gift card purchases count by purchase date. A hotel stay ending in 2027 won’t be 2026 qualifying activity because it was booked in 2026. Higher Gift Card Earnings And The Full Shopping List Rove is offering up to 30% more miles on nearly all gift cards on Black Friday. A 30% increase would turn a 5x rate into 6.5x, for instance. (The actual rate depends on the gift card.) Rove sells gift cards marked for instant mileage earning which can help with this weekend’s transfer bonuses. Earn up to $4,300 in travel value when you spend $120,000 in your first 4 months as a cardholder

As High As 175,000 points. Find Out Your Offer.

As High As 100,000 points. Find Out Your Offer.

If you fly American Airlines frequently, one of its cobranded Citi cards could save you money on your trips.

The (see rates and fees) is the only credit card that includes a full Admirals Club membership.

It also offers statement credits, a free first checked bag (on eligible domestic itineraries) and bonuses that can help you reach American Airlines AAdvantage elite status.

The card has a $695 annual fee. Whether it’s worth paying comes down to how often you’ll use the lounges and how much you’d otherwise spend on purchases covered by the card’s credits.

Apply for the : Earn 80,000 bonus miles after spending $8,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening.

Here’s how the value adds up in your first year and beyond.

New holders can currently earn 80,000 bonus miles after spending $8,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening.

This bonus is worth about $1,160, based on TPG’s November 2026 valuations. We recommend holding off until at least 100,000 miles are on offer.

A significant portion of the card's overall value comes from its bonus, so earning it and redeeming the miles wisely are crucial to offsetting the card's high annual fee.

Related: The Citi / AAdvantage Executive's new benefits are live: 6 things to do now

Arguably the most valuable ongoing benefit of this card is the complimentary Admirals Club membership you'll receive every year that you hold it. When you have the , all you have to do is walk to the lounge and present a same-day boarding pass for an eligible flight.

American charges $750 a year for a single membership, which covers Admirals Club access for one person. A full membership (with two guests) and partner lounge access costs $1,200 to $1,400 a year (depending on your AAdvantage status). If you’d otherwise pay for a full membership, the card’s $695 annual fee can be worth it for lounge access alone.

With this card, you'll be able to access almost 50 Admirals Clubs and more than 60 partner lounges worldwide when flying American or one of its Oneworld partners. Notably, this includes Alaska Airlines lounges in hubs like Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), Oregon's Portland International Airport (PDX), San Francisco International Airport (SFO) and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA).

You can bring in either your immediate family members (spouse or domestic partner and children under 18 years of age) or up to two guests. They don’t need to be on the same flight as you — just any American or Oneworld flight with a same-day boarding pass.

Related: The best lounge access credit cards to add to your wallet

The offers valuable perks when flying American, including priority check-in at business-class counters (where available) and priority boarding privileges (where available) for you and up to eight travelers on the same reservation.

You also get your first checked bag free on domestic itineraries with American Airlines, saving you at least $45 each time. (Note that this is only for domestic flights; I had to pay out of pocket when I traveled to Mexico, forgetting the restrictions of this perk.)

Additionally, you'll receive a statement credit of up to $120 for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck (once every four years). I suggest maximizing your credit by applying for Global Entry, as it includes TSA PreCheck anyway.

You'll also receive elite status with two partner programs:

Furthermore, the card includes travel protections, such as trip cancellation, trip interruption, trip delay, lost baggage protection and car rental insurance coverage.

And there are no foreign transaction fees, making this card a good option for international purchases.

Related: Which airline is now best if you don't want to pay bag fees?

If chasing AAdvantage elite status is important to you, the will help you achieve it. You’ll earn 1 Loyalty Point for every mile you earn from purchases.

Cardholders also earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points after reaching each of the following milestones in the same status qualification year:

Related: 8 methods that earned American AAdvantage Executive Platinum

The inKind dining credit is worth close to face value if you already eat at participating restaurants. Check the map for places you’d actually visit near home or on a trip.

I’ve had issues with the car rental credit, so I wouldn’t rely on it for value. Previously, a Budget rental in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, was not coded correctly, and Citi wouldn’t manually apply the credit. Later, I completed another Budget rental in Ireland and waited the obligatory 10 weeks. Again, it didn't post, and again, Citi refused to apply a manual credit.

I don’t value the Lyft perk because you don’t get the $15 credit until after you’ve taken three (nondiscounted) rides in a month. Instead, I use my (see rates and fees) to earn 5 points per dollar spent, plus a $10 monthly in-app credit on Lyft purchases (through Sept. 30, 2027).

The inflight (and Admirals Club) credit is useful if you regularly buy onboard refreshments or snacks.

Related: Frequent Uber or Lyft user? These are the best credit cards for you

If you’re looking to supercharge your points earning across several programs, I'd suggest putting your spending on a card that earns transferable points. However, if you want to maximize your AAdvantage mile balance specifically, the will earn you:

AAdvantage miles are more valuable (at 1.45 cents each) than Delta SkyMiles and United MileagePlus miles (both 1.2 cents), according to TPG's November 2026 valuations.

I redeemed part of the welcome bonus I received on this card for a luxurious flight. I used 70,000 miles (plus $174 in taxes and fees) for a one-way business-class flight in Qatar Airways’ fantastic Qsuite from Doha to Houston.

Given that this flight retails for $3,910 one-way, I got a very high 5.3 cents per mile from this redemption, more than triple TPG’s valuation of AAdvantage miles.

Related: How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles for maximum value

Finally, the is a great option if you want to extend Admirals Club access to friends and family affordably.

You can add up to three authorized users for $175 total (about $58 each), with each additional authorized user costing $175.

Every authorized user you add receives Admirals Club access (with a same-day boarding pass for an eligible flight) for themselves and up to two traveling companions. However, authorized users only get Admirals Club access, not a full Admirals Club membership.

Related: Everything you need to know about authorized credit card users

If you’d otherwise pay for a full Admirals Club membership, the card’s $695 annual fee is already less than the cost of joining directly.

The welcome bonus can add substantial value in your first year. At renewal, base your decision on how often you used the lounges and how much the credits and travel perks actually saved you.

If lounge access isn’t important to you, consider one of Citi’s lower-fee AAdvantage cards instead.

To learn more, read our full review of the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard.

#6034. Cathay Pacific Asia Miles Announces Partner Award Devaluation, Starting January 5

Starting in January, it’ll take more Cathay Pacific miles to fly British Airways first class from Los Angeles to London than to fly Cathay first class all the way from New York to Hong Kong. The London flight goes from 135,000 to 162,000 Asia Miles each way. Hong Kong stays at 160,000. For two people booking London, that’s an extra 54,000 miles one way. A week after Chase added 1:1 transfers to Cathay Pacific, Cathay tells me its partner airlines are charging it more for award seats. It’s raising the mileage price of selected partner awards and dropping Companion Ticket Awards. The new rates kick in at midnight in Hong Kong on January 5, 2027. In the U.S., get your ticket issued before 11 a.m. Eastern on Monday, January 4 (10 a.m. Central, 8 a.m. in Los Angeles) for future travel to book at the old rates. Partner Award Prices Starting January 5 These are the nine examples Cathay shared, in Asia Miles per passenger each way. The airline says its flight award search will show prices for every route and cabin starting January 5. They aren’t revealing all the changes in advance. Miles flown · Cabin Current Jan. 5 Increase Up to 750 · Economy 10,000 12,000 20% 751–2,750, Type 2 · Economy 17,500 21,000 20% 751–2,750, Type 2 · Business 37,000 44,000 18.9% 751–2,750, Type 2 · First 60,000 66,000 10% 2,751–5,000 · First 100,000 110,000 10% 5,001–7,500 · Business 93,000 100,000 7.5% 5,001–7,500 · First 135,000 162,000 20% 7,501+ · Business 120,000 130,000 8.3% 7,501+ · First 170,000 204,000 20% Hong Kong–Tokyo falls in the short “Type 2” band. Japan Airlines business class on that route goes from 37,000 to 44,000 miles. Pick the Cathay Pacific flight and it’s still 33,000 miles for the same trip. What Happens To The British Airways Surcharge Deal? One reason to use Asia Miles has been to pay less in British Airways fuel surcharges. It’s a way to save ~ $500 each way on taxes and fees between the U.S. and Europe. However, Japan Airlines generally charges fewer miles for the same award and offers equally low surcharges. JAL is a Bilt, Rove, Citibank, and Capital One transfer partner. Flying New York–London is a distance of under 5,000 miles. Cathay gave us a new first class price for that band, but hasn’t said what happens to business class. Los Angeles–London falls in the next band up. Business class there cost 89,000 miles before last May’s increase, costs 93,000 today and goes to 100,000 in January. That 100,000-mile award will take 100,000 Chase points or 125,000 American Express points. American Express gives you 800 Asia Miles per 1,000 points. Bilt, Capital One, Wells Fargo, Rove Miles and eligible Citi ThankYou cards all offer 1:1 transfers. When An American Airlines Connection Changes The Price The biggest reason I’d transfer points to Cathay is access to first and business class seats that American AAdvantage and Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards often can’t book. Last year I flagged two first class award seats at a time between New York and Hong Kong, available only with Asia Miles. I’d still check American before transferring points. Just last week Seattle and Toronto to Hong Kong opened up in business class for 70,000 American miles each way. Cathay is keeping its Standard Award prices in place. Changes are only to partner awards. New York–Hong Kong is still 119,000 miles in business class. The oneworld Multi-Carrier Award chart which covers two oneworld airlines without Cathay, or Cathay plus at least two other oneworld airlines, isn’t changing either. Cathay says very few members used its Companion Ticket Award. If work bought you a qualifying Cathay business or first class roundtrip, you could use fewer miles to bring someone along on the same flights in the same cabin. Cathay will stop issuing companion awards in January as well. If you find the partner flights you want but might need to move the trip a day, I’d ticket before the cutoff. Changes to date only preserves the ticketed mileage price, subject to award availability and any change fee. Change the route, cabin or anything else after the cutoff and the new award prices apply. One reason to use Asia Miles has been to pay less in British Airways fuel surcharges. It’s a way to save ~ $500 each way on taxes and fees between the U.S. and Europe. However, Japan Airlines generally charges fewer miles for the same award and offers equally low surcharges. JAL is a Bilt, Rove, Citibank, and Capital One transfer partner.

Flying New York–London is a distance of under 5,000 miles. Cathay gave us a new first class price for that band, but hasn’t said what happens to business class. Los Angeles–London falls in the next band up. Business class there cost 89,000 miles before last May’s increase, costs 93,000 today and goes to 100,000 in January.

That 100,000-mile award will take 100,000 Chase points or 125,000 American Express points. American Express gives you 800 Asia Miles per 1,000 points. Bilt, Capital One, Wells Fargo, Rove Miles and eligible Citi ThankYou cards all offer 1:1 transfers.

The biggest reason I’d transfer points to Cathay is access to first and business class seats that American AAdvantage and Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards often can’t book. Last year I flagged two first class award seats at a time between New York and Hong Kong, available only with Asia Miles. I’d still check American before transferring points. Just last week Seattle and Toronto to Hong Kong opened up in business class for 70,000 American miles each way. Cathay is keeping its Standard Award prices in place. #6033. Trump banks on personal relationships moving Putin, Xi toward U.S. interests

Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. (Win McNamee/AFP via Getty Images)

That was the greeting, complete with a lengthy handshake, President Donald Trump gave Vladimir Putin before two high-level meetings Thursday, including the first “trilateral” session with sitting U.S., Russian and Chinese heads of state.

“It’s nice to see you,” Trump told Putin before a private one-on-one meeting in China’s Shenzhen economic zone, before pulling the Russian strongman close and saying something into his ear too low for journalists’ microphones to pick up.

Trump and Putin then posed for the cameras with wide grins, again underscoring the U.S. president’s closeness with a world leader who has been partially shunned by the West since he launched a war with Ukraine in February 2022. Trump on Thursday also appeared several times alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, who like Putin has been scorned by Republican and Democratic lawmakers for years.

“We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We've known each other for a long time. And I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this — or, at least, start,” Trump told reporters as Putin beamed from a few feet away.

They later were joined by Xi for a group photo before sitting down at a round wooden table with a large arrangement of pink flowers in the center.

His interactions with and comments about Putin and Xi reflect Trump’s belief that his personal relationships can bend them toward U.S. interests. But that gambit clashed Thursday with his second term’s expiration date — the White House did not disclose any agreements reached during his various meetings with the two leaders, nor did Trump hold a press conference following the three-way session.

Both Putin and Xi are adept at playing the geopolitical long game. The 26 months left in Trump’s term is a relatively short amount of time compared to the duo that has been in power for a combined 56 years and will remain in place for the foreseeable future.

Indeed, even Trump acknowledged the first-ever meeting might not immediately yield much progress on its ostensible goal: paring each powers’ nuclear weapons arsenals.

“I must say, it's, quite frankly, a very hard thing to do, because once you have the nuclear weapons, it's very hard to not have them. It's very hard to give them up as the leader of a country,” Trump said as Putin and Xi looked on. “Something that's very difficult to say, because … it's the way life works.

“You know, you have thousands of weapons and you're supposed to give them up, and yet you have countries in addition to us, in much smaller numbers, but they have nuclear weapons, also,” he added. “So it's not an easy thing to do and give them up.”

Trump, who was convicted by a New York jury in a business records case and who saw a federal election interference case against him dismissed only because of his reelection, also appeared to join Putin’s resistance to international criminal justice entities that have alleged Putin has committed war crimes in Ukraine.

“In another area of potential cooperation between us, I'll be suggesting ways to protect our nations’ sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court, which has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction,” Trump said, a statement that would be almost unthinkable to hear from any other sitting U.S. president.

Other world leaders, including democratically elected ones, at two Pacific region economic summits in which Trump participated this week did not receive the kind of cordial and personal treatment from the U.S. side that Putin and Xi enjoyed.

And other world leaders and congressional Democrats this week expressed concern with Trump's closeness to the Russian and Chinese strongmen.

Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., on Thursday called the unprecedented summit a “historic embarrassment.” He criticized Trump for leaving the meeting without any apparent concrete commitments from Moscow or Beijing on a number of issues, including curbing Chinese espionage inside U.S. companies and ending the Ukraine conflict.

“This summit was nothing but a glorified photo op and a gift to Putin and Xi,” Schumer said.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote this Thursday on X, shortly after Trump’s warm greeting for the former KGB officer: “God, protect us from such friends.”

Nicolas Burns, a former senior U.S. diplomatic official under GOP and Democratic presidents, was critical of Trump’s meetings with Xi. He said it was “important” for U.S. and Chinese leaders to hold talks, but added: “We need stability in the relationship with China — but there’s a but.”

“The president seems to be following a detente policy with China, with very little substance. There’s a lot of pomp and circumstance, red carpets, a lot of nice words,” the former ambassador to China, NATO and Greece told “Morning Joe” on MS NOW. “Too friendly with Xi Jinping, who’s not going to be swayed by rosy words from President Trump.”

Even before Trump met with the Russian and Chinese leaders behind closed doors, Republican and Democratic lawmakers said they doubted very much would come from it.

“I want nuclear weapons to be reduced. As you know, China has been unwilling to even have a conversation with the United States about nuclear arms reduction until they reach a certain plateau in the number of weapons that they have,” House Armed Services Committee Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., told reporters Tuesday.

“I'm glad that they're willing to have the conversation. We do need a limit, as you know,” added Wittman, who lost his reelection bid earlier this month. “Right now, neither Russia nor China has a nuclear arms reduction treaty with the United States. It would be nice for us to actually have one.”

Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., an Armed Services Committee member, wanted Trump to press Putin over Ukraine.

“Ukraine is defending itself from Putin's aggression, which this president should be opposing as well,” Blumenthal said Tuesday. “We are spending no money on Ukraine. Let's be very clear: Arms to Ukraine are purchased by Ukraine with financial support from Europe, not America. … Let's support Ukraine.”

On spending, Trump and administration officials have been pressing Senate Republicans to quickly pass another budget reconciliation measure with $350 billion more for the Defense Department. However, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and other GOP senators have signaled in the last 24 hours that they had shelved the notion of another fast-track spending measure.

“You have to have a path forward. You've got to get on it, and you have to protect it, and that takes 50 in the Senate,” Thune told reporters Thursday. “And then you've got to get it through the House. As you probably saw yesterday, a lot of folks in the House were lobbing grenades at the Senate reconciliation bill and complaints about it not being offset, et cetera. So, you know, in my view at least, you want to have a path forward to success.”

John M. Donnelly and Jackie Wang contributed to this report.

#6032. Fiscal Reality Interrupts Everyone’s Social Security Fairy Tales

It turns out that we were right all along.

Senator Bill Cassidy (R., La.), left, President Donald Trump, right.

The most important revelation in the news that President Trump is working with his outgoing senatorial rival, Bill Cassidy, on a package of Social Security reforms is obvious: The math comes for us all, without fear or favor, and trade-offs are unavoidable even if voters hate hearing about them.

But there’s another important element to today’s news that should not go unacknowledged: We were right.

Noah Rothman is a senior writer at National Review. His third book, Blood and Progress: A Century of Left-Wing Violence, was published by Hachette in May 2026.
